title: [Platform] Agree the review rules with Nir and Tal and write them down
what: Get Nir and Tal to sign off on the review rules: any engineer may review any area, the requester never approves their own agent's PR, and every PR needs exactly 1 approval. There is no CODEOWNERS file.
why: The ruleset and the independent-approval check enforce these rules. They must be agreed before we turn them on, or the first blocked PR turns into a debate.
how: Book 30 minutes with Nir and Tal. Bring the four rules: exactly 1 approval, any area (BE can review FE and the other way around), never the requester, no CODEOWNERS.
Agree the break-glass case: Tal and Nir can merge an urgent production fix without the approval or the checks. GitHub logs every bypass, and Sean reads the list in the weekly review.
Agree who the requester of an agent PR is: the person who assigned the Jira ticket to Nova, or the routine's owner. They can't approve it, and neither can anyone who pushed a commit to it.
Write the rules as one short page (fcp docs/, or rnd-kb once G6 sets the page format) and announce it in #engineering.
Hand the agreed settings to DevOps for the ruleset (G0-02) and to Platform for the check (G0-09).

title: [DevOps] Turn on the fcp main ruleset with required unit-test checks
what: Enable fcp's disabled main-branch-protection ruleset (id 5937570) with a PR, 1 approval, stale approvals dismissed, required unit-test checks, no force-push or delete, and a logged bypass for Tal and Nir.
why: Today nothing stops a bot with write access from merging into main. Every later agent depends on this wall.
how: Make the checks requirable first. The cloud, client and frontend CI jobs are all named 'Unit Tests', and their workflows have `paths:` filters, so a required check would match the wrong job or stay pending forever. In cloud-ci.yml, client-ci.yml and frontend-ci.yaml rename the jobs to 'Cloud Unit Tests', 'Client Unit Tests' and 'Frontend Unit Tests' and remove the `paths:` filters. The existing check-changes job already skips the work, and a skipped job counts as passing.
Create the GitHub team fcp-break-glass with Tal and Nir; rulesets can't name single users as bypass actors.
Apply the ruleset with the call in the sketch, as an org admin. Export it to JSON afterwards and keep it with the review-rules page. Agents never change rulesets.
Prove it: a test PR with no approval can't merge; an FE-only PR shows the cloud and client checks as skipped and can merge after 1 approval.
The I&T gate (e2e_tests) and sdk-ci stay optional for now: the per-cloud QA locks make them too slow to require on every PR.

code.file: run once by an org admin: gh api repos/RhinoHealth/fcp/rulesets/5937570
code.text:
# Run by an org admin. Agents never change rulesets.
# 5937570 is the existing, disabled "main-branch-protection" ruleset on fcp.
TEAM_ID=$(gh api orgs/RhinoHealth/teams/fcp-break-glass --jq .id)   # Tal and Nir

gh api -X PUT repos/RhinoHealth/fcp/rulesets/5937570 --input - <<EOF
{
  "name": "main-branch-protection",
  "target": "branch",
  "enforcement": "active",
  "conditions": { "ref_name": { "include": ["refs/heads/main"], "exclude": [] } },
  "bypass_actors": [
    { "actor_type": "Team", "actor_id": ${TEAM_ID}, "bypass_mode": "pull_request" }
  ],
  "rules": [
    { "type": "deletion" },
    { "type": "non_fast_forward" },
    { "type": "pull_request", "parameters": {
        "required_approving_review_count": 1,
        "dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push": true,
        "require_last_push_approval": true,
        "require_code_owner_review": false,
        "required_review_thread_resolution": false,
        "allowed_merge_methods": ["squash"] } },
    { "type": "required_status_checks", "parameters": {
        "strict_required_status_checks_policy": false,
        "required_status_checks": [
          { "context": "Cloud Unit Tests" },
          { "context": "Client Unit Tests" },
          { "context": "Frontend Unit Tests" } ] } }
  ]
}
EOF

Name two org admins (one Security, one DevOps), the billing owner, and the workloads that get a workspace and a key: nova, routines, brain-bot. Record it in the agent inventory (G0-10).

Run a recorded 90-minute walkthrough of RhinoHealth/byte: the per-PR pipeline (gate, broker, review, sniff, finalize), fix mode, config/repositories.json, build-worker.yml signing, and the telemetry branch.
Write docs/when-it-breaks.md in the byte repo from the real failure modes (sketch).

code.text:
# When Byte breaks

Owner: Nave · Second maintainer: <name> · Alerts: #byte · Dashboard: DASHBOARD.md on the telemetry branch

## First look
1. The PR's "Byte Review" check and the caller run (byte-review.yml in the PR's repo).
2. The run artifact `byte-review-*`: the result JSON and the broker audit log.
3. `runner-canary.yml`: if the daily canary is red, the runner is the problem, not Byte.

## Symptoms
| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| No review after `@byte-review` | byte-runner-set at its max (15), or the gate skipped the PR | Look at queued jobs, then the gate log |
| Every run fails at the verify step | the main image was not signed (sign job red) | Rebuild from main; never repin by hand |
| Reviews behave like a branch build | shared `BYTE_WORKER_IMAGE` left on a branch digest | Restore the production digest |
| Every run fails at the model call | the Claude credential expired or was revoked | Rotate it as docs/setup.md says (by day 330) |
| Cost per review jumps | a prompt or playbook change, or re-review loops | Compare runs.jsonl week over week |

## Escalate
Nave, then the second maintainer. Byte is advisory: while it is down, PRs still merge with 1 approval.

title: [Nave] Hand over FCP Lab: walkthrough and a 'when it breaks' page
needs: G3 Packer image needs the Lab's images and seed data
what: Nave walks the second maintainer through FCP Lab (the fcp-local-lab repo and the fcp-lab plugin) and writes its 'when it breaks' page.
why: Agents build and test inside FCP Lab on every full-size VM. If only one person can fix it, every agent run stops when it breaks.
how: After the transfer (G0-04), run a recorded walkthrough: how lab-up boots cloud, client and frontend from a working tree, seeding, per-environment isolation, lab-doctor and lab-clean.
Write docs/when-it-breaks.md in RhinoHealth/fcp-local-lab (sketch): Docker memory and disk, port clashes between two stacks, seed failures, image pulls (Nexus, ECR), Apple silicon vs. x86.
List what G3's Packer image needs from the Lab (images, seed database, compose files) and who to ask.
Give the second maintainer write access and make them a reviewer on Lab PRs.

code.text:
# When FCP Lab breaks

Owner: Nave · Second maintainer: <name> · Runs on: laptops, and every full-size agent VM (G3)

## First look
1. `/fcp-lab:lab-doctor`: Docker engine, memory, architecture, and what already holds room.
2. `/fcp-lab:lab-clean`: what is running and what can be freed.
3. The failing service's logs in the stack's compose project.

## Symptoms
| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Stack never gets healthy | too little Docker memory, or another stack holds the ports | lab-doctor, then lab-clean the old stack |
| Seed step fails | migrations changed on the branch | <fill in from the walkthrough> |
| Image pull fails | Nexus or ECR login, or a missing image tag | <fill in from the walkthrough> |
| Works on a Mac, fails on an agent VM | arm64 vs. x86 images | <fill in from the walkthrough> |

## Escalate
Nave, then the second maintainer. On an agent VM, the run's health check (G3) stops the run
before any code is written, so a broken Lab costs time, not bad PRs.

title: [DevOps] Create the agents' ZDR org, one workspace and key per workload
needs: Anthropic account team turns on ZDR for the new org
what: Create the ZDR API organization, one workspace per workload (nova, routines, brain-bot), and one API key per workspace, stored only in Vault.
why: One key per workload gives each agent its own meter and its own kill switch: revoking one key stops one agent. Only the LLM gateway ever reads these keys.
how: With the Anthropic account team, create the org and confirm ZDR is on before any key exists.
Create workspaces nova, routines and brain-bot, and one key in each. Name keys <workspace>-gateway-<yyyymm> so rotation is visible.
Store the keys with the script in the sketch, from a laptop on VPN. Never paste a key into Jira, Slack or a file.
Note a gap for G3's threat model: the inf ClusterSecretStore vault-store can read all of kvv2, so any ExternalSecret on inf could read these keys.
Add a 90-day rotation reminder to the Vault metadata and the agent inventory.

code.file: run once by a DevOps admin on VPN: vault kv kvv2/infrastructure/ai-agents/anthropic
code.text:
# Run by a DevOps admin on VPN. Keys go only into Vault: never into a ticket, Slack or a file.
export VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.example.com
vault login -method=oidc role=terraform

SECRET=infrastructure/ai-agents/anthropic   # same layout as infrastructure/n8n
for workload in nova routines brain-bot; do  # the workload names the gateway looks up
  read -r -s -p "Anthropic API key for ${workload}: " key; echo
  # "=-" reads the value from stdin, so the key never shows in the process list or shell history
  if vault kv get -mount=kvv2 "$SECRET" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf '%s' "$key" | vault kv patch -mount=kvv2 "$SECRET" "${workload}=-"
  else
    printf '%s' "$key" | vault kv put -mount=kvv2 "$SECRET" "${workload}=-"
  fi
  unset key
done

vault kv metadata put -mount=kvv2 \
  -custom-metadata=owner=platform \
  -custom-metadata=reader=llm-gateway \
  -custom-metadata=rotate_every=90d \
  "$SECRET"

title: [DevOps] Create the rhino-ai-agents GitHub App, key in Vault, no bypass
needs: G3 broker (W3–5) is the only service that reads the key
what: Create the private GitHub App rhino-ai-agents that every AI agent pushes and opens PRs with, install it on fcp only, and keep its private key in Vault.
why: Agents need their own identity so GitHub can tell their work apart and the rules can treat it differently. Installation tokens last 1 hour and can be limited to one repo.
how: Create the App under RhinoHealth with the settings in the sketch (a record in GitHub's App manifest format): contents and pull requests write; checks, actions and metadata read. No workflows permission, so GitHub refuses any push from it that touches .github/workflows. No administration, no members.
Keep the webhook off. Agent triggers come from Jira polling, Slack and small Actions on our runners.
Install it on RhinoHealth/fcp only (Only select repositories). RhinoHealth/ai-agents is added when G4's dogfood starts.
Store app_id and the private key at kvv2 infrastructure/ai-agents/github-app, the same way as G0-07, then delete the downloaded .pem.

Check that the App is not in the fcp ruleset's bypass_actors, then mint a test token and confirm a merge of an unapproved PR fails. The broker (G3) also refuses the merge endpoint, so a person always merges.

title: [Platform] Build the independent-approval required check
needs: G3 creates RhinoHealth/ai-agents (W2); G4 hand-off and G5 routines write the Requested-by line
what: A required check that passes only when someone other than the requester approved the PR's latest commit. For agent PRs, the requester comes from the Requested-by: line the orchestrator writes in the PR body.
why: GitHub stops authors approving their own PRs, but an agent PR's author is the bot, so the person who asked for it could approve it alone. This check closes that gap.
how: Write the logic in RhinoHealth/ai-agents (`ai-agents/checks/src/independent-approval.ts`) with a reusable workflow, `ai-agents/.github/workflows/independent-approval.yml`, like Byte's review.yml. Allow org repos to call it (Settings → Actions → Access).

The reusable workflow runs the check from the ai-agents-checks image pinned by digest (`runs-on: fcp-runner-set`, `container: <inf ECR>/ai-agents-checks@sha256:…`, `run: node /app/dist/independent-approval.js`), the way Byte's review.yml runs Byte's worker image. fcp's run never has to read the private ai-agents repo, and no token is needed for it. G3-01's image job builds the image; confirm with DevOps that fcp-runner-set pulls from inf ECR.

Requesters are the PR author, the Requested-by: login on agent PRs (the routine owner for routines), anyone who pushed a commit and anyone who edited the PR body. Count only APPROVED reviews on the head commit, from people, outside that set. An agent PR without a Requested-by: line fails.

Add a thin caller in fcp, .github/workflows/independent-approval.yml, pinned by SHA: on pull_request (opened, edited, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review) and pull_request_review (submitted, edited, dismissed), with permissions contents: read and pull-requests: read.

node:test cases in `ai-agents/checks/test/independent-approval.test.ts` (run by `npm test`): a human PR approved by a teammate passes; an agent PR approved only by its requester fails; the requester edits the body then approves (fails); an approval on an older commit fails; a bot approval is ignored; a reviewer who pushed a fix is not independent.
With DevOps, add the check's exact name as GitHub shows it (for example 'independent-approval / check') to the ruleset's required checks.

title: [Platform] Write the AI agent inventory with each agent's exact access

why: The broker, the gateway and the routine charters need one answer to 'what may this agent touch'. Security reviews one file instead of five systems.
how: Create inventory/agents.yaml in RhinoHealth/ai-agents with Byte and Vanil (live) and Nova, the routines, the brain bot and the eval runner (planned).
Fill live agents from their real config: Byte from src/engines.ts and config/repositories.json, Vanil from its n8n credentials (with Nave).

For each planned agent write the narrowest set: one repo, the token permissions the broker grants, one Jira issue, one Slack thread. Routines that run unattended get no Jira writes beyond their own ticket.
Review it with Ronen. Later changes to an agent's access are PRs to this file, reviewed by Security.

title: [Platform] Narrow Vault's gha-runners role to the workflows that use it
needs: DevOps reviews (infrastructure CODEOWNERS) and a person applies; follow-up ticket replaces admin with per-workflow policies
what: Today any GitHub Actions job in any RhinoHealth repo can log in to Vault as gha-runners and get the admin policy. Bind the role to the 13 workflow files that use it today.
why: The new ai-agents repo, agent workflows and the public agent-skills repo must not be one `id-token: write` away from Vault admin. This must land before any agent workflow exists.
how: List every caller first with `gh search code gha-runners --owner RhinoHealth`. Today: 6 reusable I&T workflows in fcp, 5 workflows in infrastructure (3 ansible-*, backup-rhino-client-db, the fleetdm secrets rotator) and 2 in gitops (update-rhino-client-version).

In modules/vault/auth_backends.tf replace the `sub = repo:RhinoHealth/*` claim with the job_workflow_ref list in the sketch. Leave the duplicate jwt mount resources and the admin policy alone in this change.
A person runs plan and apply over VPN. Rerun one job per repo (an fcp I&T job, an infrastructure molecule test, a gitops staging update) and confirm a job from any other repo is now refused.

Open the follow-up for DevOps (about 1 day): one role per workflow group with a least-privilege policy (fcp I&T reads QA secrets only; the rotator and molecule leases write their own paths) instead of admin.

code.text:
# infrastructure/modules/vault/auth_backends.tf
# Before: sub = "repo:RhinoHealth/*" gave admin to any job in any org repo, the public agent-skills repo included.
# Now: only the 13 workflow files that log in with this role today. A new caller needs a reviewed change here.
# Refs stay open (@*) because the fcp I&T workflows run on every branch push.
locals {
  gha_runner_workflows = [
    "RhinoHealth/fcp/.github/workflows/_cloud-int-tests-reusable-*.yml@*",
    "RhinoHealth/fcp/.github/workflows/_client-int-tests-reusable-*.yml@*",
    "RhinoHealth/fcp/.github/workflows/_frontend-int-tests-reusable-*.yml@*",
    "RhinoHealth/infrastructure/.github/workflows/ansible-molecule-test.yml@*",
    "RhinoHealth/infrastructure/.github/workflows/ansible-molecule-test-everything.yml@*",
    "RhinoHealth/infrastructure/.github/workflows/ansible-run-playbook.yml@*",
    "RhinoHealth/infrastructure/.github/workflows/backup-rhino-client-db.yml@*",
    "RhinoHealth/infrastructure/.github/workflows/scheduled-fleedm-enrollment-secrets-rotator.yml@*",
    "RhinoHealth/gitops/.github/workflows/_update-rhino-client-version-batch.yml@*",
    "RhinoHealth/gitops/.github/workflows/update-rhino-client-version-staging.yml@*",
  ]
}

resource "vault_jwt_auth_backend_role" "gha_runners" {
  backend   = vault_jwt_auth_backend.github_actions.path
  role_name = "gha-runners"
  role_type = "jwt"

  user_claim        = "sub"
  bound_audiences   = ["https://github.com/RhinoHealth"]
  bound_claims_type = "glob"
  bound_claims = {
    # job_workflow_ref is the file the job runs in, so reusable workflows match whoever calls them.
    job_workflow_ref = join(",", local.gha_runner_workflows) # comma-separated = "any of these"
  }

  token_policies = ["admin"] # unchanged in this step; least-privilege policies are the follow-up
  token_ttl      = 3600
}

title: [Platform] Managed settings: keep model defaults, Fable and agent teams off
needs: G3's Packer image bakes the same file for agents; G8 (W7) adds plugin settings next to it
what: Ship one small managed-settings file that blocks Fable models and keeps agent teams off, and change nothing else: people keep Anthropic's model and effort defaults.
why: Fable needs 30-day data retention, a compliance call we have not made, and it is not available under ZDR. Every other model choice stays with the person.
how: Keep the source in RhinoHealth/ai-agents at settings/managed-settings.d/10-models.json, so every change is a reviewed PR.

People: paste it into claude.ai Admin Settings → Claude Code managed settings (server-managed). Agents: G3's Packer image copies it to /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.d/, because sessions that sign in with a Console API key don't receive server-managed settings.
Don't set availableModels, model or effortLevel. Subagents and workflows keep using the session's model.
deniedModels needs Claude Code v2.1.283 or later. Check on a laptop: /model shows Fable hidden or greyed out, and /status lists the managed source.

title: [Platform] LLM gateway: stream calls to Anthropic with the workload's key
needs: G3 creates RhinoHealth/ai-agents (W2); G3's orchestrator mints a run token per run
what: A small TypeScript reverse proxy for the Anthropic Messages API (`node:http` and `fetch`, like Byte's broker). It checks a short-lived run token, adds the Anthropic key for that workload, and streams the response back untouched.
why: The sandbox VM must never hold the Anthropic key. Anthropic's hosting guide recommends exactly this: a proxy that injects the key.
how: Create the gateway workspace in RhinoHealth/ai-agents (`ai-agents/gateway/`, TypeScript on Node 24: `node:http` and global `fetch`, no web framework, like Byte's broker). Routes: POST /v1/messages and /v1/messages/count_tokens, and GET /health for the pod probes; anything else returns 404. The query string passes through. Request bodies are read whole with no 1 MiB cap (unlike Byte's broker): a long session's request is several MB, and Anthropic caps the size itself.

Image `ai-agents-llm-gateway`, built by `ai-agents/.github/workflows/images.yml` like Byte's Dockerfile: `FROM node:24-bookworm-slim@sha256:…` (pinned by digest), `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, `tsc` build, non-root user 10001, `CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"]`. Port 8080 for the API, 9090 for metrics (next ticket).

Run tokens are HMAC-signed (`src/auth.ts`: `createHmac("sha256")`, checked with `timingSafeEqual`) and carry agent, jira, run, expiry and a per-agent epoch; the signing key lives at kvv2 infrastructure/ai-agents/gateway. A `mint-token` script (`src/mint-token.ts`) is for tests; the token is not an Anthropic key and dies with the run.
Kill switch: a disabled_agents setting, and bumping an agent's epoch kills all its live tokens.
Never touch content: no body logging, an access log with method, path, status and latency only, and a node:test case (`gateway/test/server.test.ts`) that fails if any request text reaches the logs.
Pass 429 and 529 through with retry-after; the harness waits and retries. The gateway never refuses a call over budget.

Client settings for the harness: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN (the run token), ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true and CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FINE_GRAINED_TOOL_STREAMING=1, because both are off by default behind a gateway. Test with `claude -p` and the Agent SDK, streaming and not.

title: [Platform] LLM gateway: meter spend per run and ticket, export metrics
needs: G3 harness reads the spend endpoint for its backstop (shadow mode first)
what: Count tokens and cost for every call from the response's usage numbers, tag them by agent, Jira key, run and step, export them as metrics, and answer 'how much has this run spent' for the harness.
why: The harness pauses between turns when a run passes its far-away backstop, and the weekly review needs cost per ticket. The gateway is the one meter an agent can't change.
how: Parse usage from both shapes: the JSON body of a non-streaming call, and the message_start and message_delta SSE events (output_tokens there is a running total).

Price table `ai-agents/gateway/prices.yaml` (loaded by `src/prices.ts` with `yaml`), $ per million tokens: Opus 5.5 input 4, output 20, cache write 5 (5 min) or 8 (1 h), cache read 0.20; Sonnet 5.5 2, 10, 2.50 or 4, 0.10; Haiku 5.5 0.10, 0.50, 0.125 or 0.20, 0.01 up to 100K-token prompts. Split 1-hour writes with usage.cache_creation. An unknown model counts tokens and raises an alert; the call never fails.

Export Prometheus metrics with @prometheus-io/client (prom-client's new name) on :9090: ai_agents_llm_tokens_total{agent,model,type,step} and ai_agents_llm_cost_usd_total{agent,model,jira,run,step}. That client doesn't add `_total`, so the names carry it. The run label is fine at a few hundred runs a month.

GET /v1/spend?run=… or ?jira=… returns the total from VictoriaMetrics (a `fetch` to vmselect at SPEND_QUERY_URL), so it survives restarts. A 30-second scrape delay is fine for a backstop checked between turns.
The backstop decision stays in the harness (G3), in shadow mode for 4 weeks. The gateway reports; it never refuses.

title: [DevOps] Deploy the LLM gateway on inf-rhinohealth with a spend alert
needs: G3 decides how sandbox VMs reach the gateway (no VPC peering); G1 dashboards read its metrics
what: Run the gateway on inf-rhinohealth as a Terraform helm_release unit (like n8n), with its keys from Vault, an internal route, metrics scraping, and an alert when an agent's day looks unusual.
why: Agents and the brain bot need one stable address for Claude, and someone has to hear about a runaway day before the invoice arrives.
how: Add ECR repo ai-agents-llm-gateway (tags_immutability_enabled = true) to multi_tenant/accounts/infrastructure/artifacts/artifacts.hcl. The ai-agents repo's images.yml builds it (node:24-bookworm-slim pinned by digest, user 10001, `CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"]`) and pushes it.

Create modules/ai-agents-service: a small local chart (Deployment, Service, HTTPRoute, ExternalSecret from vault-store, VMServiceScrape), shaped like modules/goalert/chart. Pods keep the image's command, run as user 10001 with a read-only root filesystem, and probe GET /health. G3's broker, workers and Slack app reuse it.
Add the unit in the sketch. Set the HTTPRoute request timeout to 0s (n8n sets 300s); long streams would be cut otherwise.

Add victoria-metrics/alerting/templates/alert_rules/ai-agents.yml: AIAgentDailySpendUnusual when `sum by (agent) (increase(ai_agents_llm_cost_usd_total[1d]))` is above 2× its 14-day average. Route service.name=ai-agents to a new Slack receiver for #ai-agents-alerts (the plan's #agents-alerts, renamed so it isn't confused with the Rhino agents channel).
A person runs plan and apply. Smoke test: `claude -p 'say ok'` through the gateway from a pod in the cluster, then find its cost series in Grafana.

title: [Platform] Spend visibility and far-away ceilings for people and agents
needs: G3's orchestrator holds new runs above 90% of a workspace limit; G1 builds the Grafana spend view
what: Turn on spend visibility for each person, set alerts on the R&D pool, give each agent workspace a far monthly limit with alerts, and book the date when the per-person ceiling is set from real data.
why: We want to see spend before we limit it. No limit may cut a run in the middle, so ceilings are far away, start in shadow mode and are set from 4 weeks of data.
how: People: confirm each person sees their own spend with /usage and the status line, and nobody sees a per-person list. In the Claude admin console, set R&D pool alerts at 50, 75 and 95% (Enterprise).

No per-person caps during W3–W7. Book 30 minutes on 18 Nov (W7) with Ronen to set the extra-usage limit at about 3× a heavy user's real month (first guess about $500), with the first 'request more' each month approved automatically.
Agents: in the ZDR org set each workspace's monthly limit at about 3× expected spend, with alerts at 50, 75 and 90% to #ai-agents-alerts.
Write the numbers in settings/spend-limits.yaml (sketch). The orchestrator reads hold_new_runs_above_pct: above 90%, new runs wait in the queue while running ones finish.

code.text:
# ai-agents/settings/spend-limits.yaml
# Far-away limits only. Each one logs what it would have done for 4 weeks (shadow) before it can act.
# No limit stops a run in the middle: limits act before a run starts or between turns.
mode: shadow
people:
  observe_until: 2026-11-18            # end of W7: no new caps before this
  extra_usage_limit_usd: null          # set in W7 at ~3x a heavy user's real month (first guess ~500)
  first_request_more_each_month: auto_approve
  later_requests: a lead approves the same day
  rnd_pool_alerts_pct: [50, 75, 95]    # Enterprise R&D pool
  visibility: own spend only (/usage, status line); team totals in Grafana, never names
agents:                                # one ZDR workspace and one gateway workload each
  nova:      { monthly_limit_usd: null, alerts_pct: [50, 75, 90], hold_new_runs_above_pct: 90 }
  routines:  { monthly_limit_usd: null, alerts_pct: [50, 75, 90], hold_new_runs_above_pct: 90 }
  brain-bot: { monthly_limit_usd: null, alerts_pct: [50, 75, 90], hold_new_runs_above_pct: 90 }
  # monthly_limit_usd: about 3x expected spend, filled in when the workspace limit is set
burn_rate_alert:                       # built in G1 (spend view)
  ahead_of_budget_pct: 25
  notify: [sean, nir]

title: [Platform] Second maintainer ships one real change to Byte and to the Lab
what: The second maintainer picks one small real change in Byte and one in FCP Lab, ships both through normal review, and fixes the 'when it breaks' pages where they were wrong.
why: A walkthrough isn't a handover. Shipping a change proves the second maintainer can build, test and deploy both tools without Nave.
how: Pick from the real backlog with Nave: a Byte ROADMAP.md item or open issue, and a Lab issue, each under half a day.
Byte: npm ci and npm run check, try it on a branch image as the README's Deploying section says, restore BYTE_WORKER_IMAGE afterwards, merge, and watch the main build sign and repin.
Lab: make the change, boot a full stack with lab-up, run lab-review on the change, merge.
Nave reviews but doesn't drive. Fix both 'when it breaks' pages wherever reality differed.

title: [Platform] Locked checks: block agent PRs that edit CI, lint or QA checks
needs: G3 broker keeps the PR body's locked-checks block read-only; G4 'checks first' writes the block
what: A required check that fails an agent PR if it changes CI workflows, lint, type or test config, or the QA checks approved in its plan.
why: An agent must not pass by weakening its test. Agents can't weaken the checks they are judged by, and GitHub enforces it, not a prompt.
how: The first wall is already there: the rhino-ai-agents App has no workflows permission, so GitHub refuses its pushes to .github/workflows.

Add `ai-agents/checks/src/locked-checks.ts` next to `independent-approval.ts`, with fcp's list kept in ai-agents/settings/protected-paths.yaml (one block per repo; the harness hooks in G3-21 read the same file), and run it as a second job in fcp's caller (`node /app/dist/locked-checks.js` in the same ai-agents-checks image). Human PRs pass straight through.

fcp's pyproject.toml is only partly locked: agents may change dependencies, not [tool.black], [tool.isort] or coverage settings. Compare the parsed sections (smol-toml, then `isDeepStrictEqual`), not the text.
QA checks approved in the plan: read the file list from the <!-- ai-agents:locked-checks --> block the orchestrator writes in the PR body. Until G4 writes it, only the static list applies.
Eval sets live in the restricted golden-set repo, which the agent's one-repo token never covers, so they need no entry here. Add the check to the fcp ruleset's required checks with DevOps.

Lock fcp's verify entry points too (.claude/settings.json with its Stop hook, scripts/claude_stop_verify.sh, scripts/poe_verify.py, frontend/scripts/verify.ts from G7), so an agent can't change the check that judges it.

title: [Platform] Flag weakened tests: removed asserts, new skips, looser limits
needs: G4's scope judge reads the same findings
what: A check on every PR that calls out test edits which weaken checks: removed assertions, new skips or .only, and loosened thresholds. It annotates the diff; it doesn't block.
why: Edits to existing tests are allowed, because tests change with the code. The one reviewer must still see when a change makes a test easier to pass.
how: Add `ai-agents/checks/src/weakened-tests.ts` and run it as a third job in fcp's caller (`node /app/dist/weakened-tests.js` in the same ai-agents-checks image), on every PR (people and agents).

fcp test files: frontend/test/unit/**, frontend/e2e/**, **/tests/**, cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoCore/integration-tests/**. Thresholds: coverage fail-under, vitest coverage thresholds, Playwright retries and timeouts.
Output: one ::warning annotation per finding on its file, plus a short job summary. No PR comment, so no write permission is needed.
Calibrate on the last 50 merged fcp PRs: at most one false alarm per ten PRs, or drop the noisy pattern.
Also write the findings as JSON in the job output, so G4's scope judge and the PR story can quote them.
